page: Amazon Web Services c8a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance powered by the AWS Nitro System and an AMD EPYC 9R45 processor. It provides 8 dedicated physical cores running at up to 4.5 GHz with one thread per core and no simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance is equipped with 16 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 6 GHz, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It includes 32 MB of L3 cache, a 4 Gbps baseline network capability, and does not include local instance storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-thread processing capabilities, with the AMD EPYC architecture placing in the top 10% for single-core stress-ng, Geekbench single-core (2,803 points), gzip compression, and text processing. Multi-core performance across stress-ng and Geekbench lands in the median 50% tier, consistent with an 8-core allocation. Memory read bandwidth registers at 54.59 GB/s for large uncached blocks, while lightweight neural network inference tests display top-tier generation rates for small 135M parameter models.

The hardware configuration provides high compute density per core, making it cost-efficient for workloads that demand high per-thread execution speed rather than expansive memory capacity. Because local storage is absent, all persistent input and output depends on network-attached storage over the Nitro architecture.

The c8a.2xlarge instance is structured for compute-bound tasks that prioritize single-thread throughput, such as Clang compilation, static web serving pipelines, microservice backend clusters, video or image processing routines, and continuous integration runners.
